results.title: Explains part 2 in plain words for a non-physicist
results.idealItem: Presenter (explains a part) + Knowing when to talk
results.chapter: Meeting 3: Understanding the results and observations (parts 2 and 3)
results.asked: Suppose someone joins who hasn't done physics since school. How would you explain what this part says, in plain words?Suppose someone joins who hasn't done physics since school. How would you explain what this part says, in plain words?
results.answer: you set theta to ninety degrees, horizontal velocity is zero so the projectile just goes straight up and down. The max height becomes v naught squared over two g, and the flight time is two v naught over g, with zero range. Sure. First, the path is a parabola, a symmetric arc through where it starts. If it's launched and lands at the same height, the total time in the air comes from setting the height back to zero and solving for the time. The maximum height comes when the upward speed has dropped to zero, and the range comes from multiplying the horizontal speed by that flight time. And it turns out the range depends on sine two theta, so complementary angles give the same distance.
results.why: It omits the 45° maximum-range result, speed-squared scaling, and mass independence; it also uses “sine two theta” without an everyday explanation.
